about_app_calendar_note: Encrypted on-device calendar with natural-language scheduling and to-do lists.
about_app_commander_note: On-device voice assistant — wake word, speech-to-text, and instant voice-shortcut rules you define yourself.
about_app_expenses_note: Encrypted on-device expense tracker — voice, receipt scan, or automatic capture.
about_app_hub_note: Backup, restore, and cloud-free peer-to-peer sync across the family of apps.
about_app_notes_note: Encrypted on-device notes, created by voice or by hand.
about_app_vision_note: Privacy-first document scanner and live text reader, with on-device OCR.
about_every_dependency_and_every_asset_i: Every dependency and every asset is listed in docs/licensing.md in the repository, with its licence and whether it is compatible. The core build carries no non-free asset at all.
about_inference_uses_llama_cpp_mit_licen: Inference uses llama.cpp, MIT licensed, compiled from source. Models are not bundled; the ones this build will load are Apache-2.0 and are imported by you from a file.
about_other_apps_note: Other free and open-source Android apps by the same author, all in one repository.
about_plus_note: A separate application with an on-device text assistant: a draft box above the keys whose contents a model can correct, translate, re-tone or shorten. It takes no permissions either, and bundles no model — one arrives only when you pick a file yourself. Installing it does not replace this one; the two run side by side and keep separate settings.
about_plus_repository_note: The repository gives you updates. The file is a one-off, and you would come back here for the next version.
about_the_commit_above_is_the_one: The commit above is the one this binary was built from. Opening the link hands it to your browser; this app holds no network permission of its own.
about_you_may_use_study_change_and: You may use, study, change and share this. If you distribute a changed version, you pass the same freedoms on with it.
assistant_a_gguf_file_is_not_a: A GGUF file is not a document — it is weights that a runtime maps and executes in a process holding your selected text. So a file is accepted only if its SHA-256 matches one of these, taken from the publishing repository's own metadata. Anything else is refused and deleted.
assistant_copying_and_hashing_a_model_is: Copying and hashing. A model is hundreds of megabytes; this takes a while.
assistant_in_a_separate_process_started_: In a separate process, started when you ask for something and stopped ninety seconds after you stop. The keyboard never loads a model: a process holding several hundred megabytes is the first thing Android reclaims, and the keyboard has to still be there when you tap the next text field.
assistant_it_is_reached_only_from_a: It is reached only from a text selection, never from what you are typing, and it is refused outright in a password field. Nothing it produces is inserted until you press Replace.
assistant_mb_needs_about_mb_of_ram:
%s MB · %s · needs about %s MB of RAM

sha256 %s…
assistant_model_eurollm_17b_note: Trained specifically for balanced coverage across the languages of the EU, rather than English first and everything else after. A better choice for translation quality at roughly the same size as the Qwen3 1.7B build above.
assistant_model_eurollm_9b_note: The largest here, and expected to be the most capable at any task in a European language -- at a real cost: several times the memory of every other entry on this list, workable only on a phone with a lot of RAM to spare.
assistant_model_qwen3_06b_note: The smallest and fastest of these. General-purpose; like the others below except EuroLLM, its training leans English, so translating into a less-common language is its weakest task.
assistant_model_qwen3_17b_note: Larger than the 0.6B build of the same model, with room for a longer chain of reasoning. Still general-purpose, still English-leaning.
assistant_model_smollm3_3b_note: The largest general-purpose option here. Also English-leaning in training, which shows most on a task that asks it to write fluently in another language rather than just read one.
assistant_no_model_imported_yet_settings: No model imported yet. Settings › Text assistant.
assistant_refused_this_file_hashes_to_wh: Refused. This file hashes to %s…, which is not a model this build knows. The copy has been deleted.
assistant_still_working_on_the_previous_: Still working on the previous request.
assistant_switched_off_the_file_no_longe: Switched off: the file no longer matches its recorded hash.
assistant_switching_model_reloads_it: A model is loaded when first used and dropped after ninety seconds of silence. Pointing a task at a different one means it loads when you switch to that kind of task — a few seconds each time.
assistant_temperature_note: How far the model is allowed to wander from the single most likely next word. Low keeps it close to literal and predictable; high lets rarer, more inventive continuations through. 0.3 is the default -- deliberately low, because every task here transforms text you already wrote rather than inventing new text.
assistant_the_assistant_does_nothing_unt: The assistant does nothing until one is imported. Nothing is downloaded; you choose a file.
assistant_the_file_could_not_be_read: The file could not be read.
assistant_the_model_could_not_be_loaded: The model could not be loaded. It may not fit in memory on this device.
assistant_the_model_file_changed_since_i: The model file changed since it was imported and was not loaded.
assistant_the_model_is_imported_and_work: The model has its own copy now and works independently of it. Delete the file you picked to reclaim its space, or keep it -- nothing about the model changes either way. Not every file picker supports this; if it does not, nothing happens.
assistant_the_selection_is_longer_than_t: The selection is longer than this model's context window.
assistant_top_p_note: How wide a slice of likely next words the model may choose from, cut off once their combined probability passes this fraction. Low keeps the choice to a handful of safe continuations; high opens it to more of the tail. 0.9 is the default.
backup_error_damaged: That file is damaged and cannot be read.
backup_error_needs_passphrase: This file is encrypted. Enter its passphrase.
backup_error_not_a_backup: That file was not written by this application.
backup_error_wrong_passphrase: That passphrase does not open this file.
backup_import_note: What a file brings is added to what is here rather than replacing it: the two dictionaries are merged word by word, so nothing this device already knew is lost. Settings are the exception — they arrive as one set.
backup_part_clipboard_note: Text only, never images. It is deliberately short-lived here; a file outlives it.
backup_part_dictionary_note: Every word and word pair this device learned from what you typed, and the words you refused. The most useful thing to carry to another install, and the most revealing thing in this application.
backup_part_languages_note: Which languages are switched on and their weights. Not the dictionaries themselves — those are inside the application and get added from it.
backup_part_settings_note: Theme, size and placement, layout, corrections, the draft box and its kept instructions, and which text-assistant model is active.
backup_passphrase_needed: The dictionary and the clipboard live in an encrypted database, so a file carrying either is encrypted too. Choose a passphrase — without it the file cannot be read, by you or anyone else.
backup_passphrase_not_needed: Nothing private is included, so the file is written plainly and needs no passphrase.
clipboard_clear_after_insert_note: Clears the clipboard right after you paste from it.
clipboard_clear_on_close: Forget everything when the keyboard closes
clipboard_clear_on_close_note: Clears everything unpinned the moment you leave the text field.
clipboard_delete_after_use: Delete this item after it is used
clipboard_delete_after_use_note: Deletes an item from the history the moment you paste it, unless it is pinned.
clipboard_expired_items_are_deleted_not_: Expired items are deleted, not merely hidden. Filtering them out of the list would leave the text sitting in the database for anything that got hold of the file.
clipboard_only_while_borderkeys_is_the_k: Only while BorderKeys is the active keyboard.
clipboard_remember_images_note: Also remembers copied images and screenshots, not just text. Turning it off deletes any already saved.
clipboard_retention_note: How far back the history reaches. Both limits apply: an entry goes when it is older than this, or when it is pushed off the end of the list, whichever happens first.
clipboard_size_note: The oldest goes when the list is full, whatever its timer says. Pinned entries do not count against this and are never dropped for age.
common_reset_to_defaults_note: Puts every setting on this screen back to what it started as. Nothing outside this screen changes.
composer_empty: Write here. Nothing reaches the app until you insert it.
composer_no_saved_prompts: Nothing kept yet. Write a prompt, and it can be kept once it has worked.
composer_prompt_hint: What should be done to this text?
composer_settings_bar_note: Up to eight, in the order you put them. The two arrows that step through the versions are always at the ends and are not in this list. Everything but insert needs a model installed, and is not drawn when there is none.
composer_settings_enable_note: Adds a Compose button to the quick actions row. Tapping it opens the draft box in its own screen, apart from whatever you were typing into.
composer_settings_none: No buttons. Insert is drawn anyway, or the box would have no way out but the cross.
composer_settings_saved_note: Written in the box and kept after they worked. The name is what fits on a button; the instruction under it is what is sent.
composer_settings_snap_selection: Grow a selection to whole words
composer_settings_snap_selection_note: Before an action runs on part of the text, a selection that starts or ends inside a word is pushed out to the word's edge, so a model always gets a whole phrase.
corrections_a_correction_is_only_learned: A correction is only learned once it survives that first backspace. Reject it and nothing is remembered except your own word, which is what rejecting it says.
corrections_apply_the_first_suggestion_w: Apply the first suggestion when you press space
corrections_backspace_puts_back_what_you: Backspace puts back what you typed
corrections_capitalise_note: Capitalises the first letter of a sentence, word, or every letter — whichever the field you're typing in asks for.
corrections_clipboard_once_note: The chip goes as soon as you use it, or when the keyboard closes. What you copied stays in the history panel — this is about the row above the keys, not about forgetting anything.
corrections_correction_strictness_note: 1.0 is the engine's own calibrated default. Lower it and a correction needs a smaller frequency gap to win, so more of what you type gets corrected -- including some that should not have been. Raise it and the gap has to be bigger, so corrections get rarer and closer to certain.
corrections_double_space: Two spaces make a full stop
corrections_double_space_note: Only after a word, and only when the second space follows the first quickly. Undone by the backspace after it, like every other substitution here.
corrections_min_correction_length_note: Words shorter than this are left alone even with correcting turned on -- a short word is the one most likely to already be a different real word, so a guess there is the most likely to be wrong.
corrections_off_by_default_with_it_off: Off by default. With it off, space commits exactly the letters you typed and a correction is applied only when you tap it.
corrections_offer_the_clipboard_note: Puts what is on the clipboard in the first slot of the strip, as a photo or as the first few words of the text. It takes one of the suggestion slots rather than adding one, and it is only ever offered — nothing is pasted until you tap it. Never in a password field.
corrections_offers_vreau_s_where_it_woul: Offers a two-word phrase where it would otherwise offer only the first of them, for the phrases you write over and over.
corrections_only_from_what_you_have_writ: Only from what you have written, never from the dictionary: frequency can chain any two common pairs into something grammatical and meaningless. The second word needs twice the evidence of the first, so a phrase appears after about four repetitions where a single word appears after two — twice the evidence for twice the guess. The first word is always offered on its own as well.
corrections_space_after_note: Adds the space you were going to type after a full stop, comma, question or exclamation mark. Pressing space yourself right after is swallowed rather than doubled.
corrections_space_before_note: A space in front of a full stop is not something anyone means, and it is what a keyboard that adds spaces produces if it does not also take them back. Only for marks that close up against the word — a dash or a bracket often wants the space.
corrections_the_backspace_straight_after: The backspace straight after a correction restores your original word instead of deleting a letter. One key, and it is exactly as you wrote it.
corrections_the_row_above_the_keys_it: The row above the keys. Turning it off does not just hide the row -- it stops the keyboard from computing suggestions or corrections at all, for someone who wants nothing but the keys.
corrections_the_strip_is_a_fixed_width: The strip is a fixed width, so every extra slot makes each one narrower and each target smaller. The preview above uses words of realistic length rather than short filler, because that is where the difference shows.
corrections_the_usual_objection_to_autoc: The usual objection to autocorrect is not that it is wrong sometimes — it is that undoing it costs more than typing the word did. So this only exists together with the switch below, and the shortest word it will touch is its own setting, further down.
dictionary_a_blocked_word_is_never_sugge: A blocked word is never suggested again. Blocking also forgets it: deleting alone would let the word come straight back from the language pack.
dictionary_a_phrase_written_twice_starts: A phrase written twice starts to lead. What the dictionary predicts stays in the strip behind it.
dictionary_a_word_is_learned_when_you: A word is learned when you choose it from the suggestion strip. Nothing is learned from what you merely typed, and nothing at all in a password field.
dictionary_about_six_repetitions_before_: About six repetitions before a phrase you write outranks what the dictionary predicts. The keyboard will not rearrange itself around one sentence you wrote once.
dictionary_off_means_nothing_new_is_reco: Off means nothing new is recorded. What has already been learned stays until you delete it below.
dictionary_showing_the_first_200_use_sea: Showing the first 200. Use search to narrow it down.
dictionary_the_file_could_not_be_read: The file could not be read.
dictionary_the_first_time_counts_best_if: The first time counts. Best if you write the same things every day; it does mean a one-off phrase leads until you write something else.
dictionary_this_does_not_change_what_is: This does not change what is recorded — every word and pair you confirm is stored either way. It changes how soon what you write starts leading the suggestion strip instead of what the dictionary says.
dictionary_this_is_the_only_form_of: This is the only form of sync there is. The app cannot reach a network, so a file you carry is the only way anything moves.
home_backup: Write what this keyboard knows to a file, or read one back
home_borderkeys_requests_no_permissions_: BorderKeys requests no permissions and contains no code that can open a network connection. Nothing it learns leaves this device.
home_colours_corners_and_spacing_with_a: Colours, corners and spacing, with a live preview
home_draft_box: A place to write that the app cannot see, and what the model may do to it
home_enabled_but_another_keyboard_is_sti: Enabled, but another keyboard is still the default.
home_height_one_handed_mode_floating_and: Height, one-handed mode, floating, and how far off the bottom edge
home_history_pinning_and_how_long_it: History, pinning and how long it is kept
home_quick_actions_note: A row of buttons for copying, pasting and selecting
home_sound_and_vibration_note: A sound or a buzz on every key press
home_summarise_correct_and_translate_on_: Summarise, correct and translate, on this device
home_the_keyboard_is_not_enabled_in: The keyboard is not enabled in system settings yet.
home_the_suggestion_strip_autocorrect_an: The suggestion strip, autocorrect, and swipe typing.
home_what_is_stored_where_and_what: What is stored, where, and what is not
home_which_dictionaries_are_active_and_t: Which dictionaries are active, and their weights
home_which_keys_and_where_separate_from: The number row, accents, key size, long-press timing, and which layouts are enabled.
languages_a_pack_s_header_is_validated: A pack's header is validated completely before any of it is mapped — magic, version, checksum, and every section offset against the real file size. A pack that does not pass is refused rather than interpreted.
languages_gpl_3_0_or_later_the: GPL-3.0-or-later — the word list is written in this repository
languages_interface_explanation: Which language this app and the keyboard's own labels are written in. Separate from the dictionaries above: reading the interface in one language while writing in another is common, so the two are not tied together.
languages_lock_evidence_note: Evidence is counted in words that only one of your dictionaries knows. Words that several of them share settle nothing, and they are most of a sentence. Patient waits for about six telling words, Quick decides on the first. What you have written yourself is never filtered: a phrase you repeat outranks any guess about the sentence.
languages_lock_explanation: Once a few words identify the language, the other dictionaries stop being consulted. Without this, the most frequent words of one language outrank the mid-frequency words of another, and a sentence in one language keeps being offered words from a different one.
languages_lock_off_note: Every dictionary is consulted for every word. Right for writing two languages inside one sentence.
languages_lock_strict_note: Nothing is ever offered from a language that has not been recognised in what you are writing. Before anything is recognised it uses the dictionary you weighted highest, on its own, and switches as soon as the evidence says otherwise. The other settings all consult every dictionary until they have decided; this one does not.
languages_not_recorded_set_by_whoever_bu: not recorded — set by whoever built the pack
languages_nothing_is_downloaded_ever_add: Nothing is downloaded, ever. Add one of the dictionaries below, which are inside the application, or import a file you built yourself with tools/build_dict.py from a word list whose licence you know.
languages_off_by_default_it_stores_a: Remembers which languages you tend to use in each app, so it can prioritise them automatically. Turning it off deletes what was learned.
languages_remember_which_languages_you_u: Remember which languages you use in which app
languages_restart_note: Applied to the keyboard the next time it opens, and to this screen straight away.
languages_stick_to_one_language: Stick to the language you are writing in
languages_switched_itself_off_the_file_n: Switched itself off: the file no longer matches the hash it was imported with.
languages_the_bundled_dictionary_could_n: The bundled dictionary could not be read.
languages_the_bundled_dictionary_is_not_: The bundled dictionary is not valid: %s. This is a bug.
languages_the_file_could_not_be_read: The file could not be read.
languages_these_are_in_the_application_i: These are in the application itself, not on a server — there is no network here to fetch anything from. Adding one copies it out of the app and validates it exactly like a file you chose.
languages_words_written_in_this_reposito: %s words, written in this repository. A starter: enough for everyday words, and meant to be replaced by a dictionary compiled from a real corpus.
layout_a_layout_and_a_language_are: The keyboard has one QWERTY. Which accents appear on the letters comes from the languages you enable in Languages, not from the layout. Up to four dictionaries are consulted at once, so having several active is normal.
layout_accented_characters_note: Hold a letter to reach the accents of the languages you have turned on. Turn a language off and its accents go with it.
layout_enable_borderkeys_first_then_its_: Enable BorderKeys first, then its layouts appear here.
layout_large_key_text_note: Bigger letters on the keys, at the cost of the wide labels being squeezed to fit.
layout_long_press_hints_note: The small character in a key's corner showing what holding it would type.
layout_number_row_note: A row of digits above the letters. Without it, holding a letter on the top row types the digit above it.
layout_resize_note: Height, width, one-handed mode, and where the keyboard sits.
layout_the_globe_key_cycles_between_the: The globe key cycles between the layouts you enabled above, without leaving BorderKeys.
layout_where_the_digits_sit: Where the digits sit on the symbols page
pack_a_hash_capacity_is_not_a: a hash capacity is not a power of two
pack_a_section_is_the_wrong_size: a section is the wrong size for what it holds
pack_a_section_points_outside_the_file: a section points outside the file
pack_the_content_checksum_does_not_match: the content checksum does not match, so the file is damaged
pack_the_counts_in_the_header_contradict: the counts in the header contradict each other
pack_the_file_could_not_be_opened: the file could not be opened
pack_the_file_could_not_be_opened_2: the file could not be opened: %s
pack_the_file_is_larger_than_a: the file is larger than a language pack may be
pack_the_file_is_too_small_to: the file is too small to contain a pack header
pack_the_file_size_does_not_match: the file size does not match what the header declares, so it is truncated or padded
pack_the_header_checksum_does_not_match: the header checksum does not match
pack_the_header_is_the_wrong_size: the header is the wrong size
pack_the_pack_was_built_for_a: the pack was built for a different format version
pack_this_is_not_a_borderkeys_language: this is not a BorderKeys language pack
privacy_clipboard_history_the_personal_d: Clipboard history, the personal dictionary and the list of imported packs live in a SQLCipher database. Its key is generated on this device and held by the Android Keystore, so the file is useless if it is copied elsewhere.
privacy_cloud_backup_and_device_to_devic: Cloud backup and device-to-device transfer are both switched off for this app. Moving your dictionary to a new phone is an explicit CSV export.
privacy_haptic_feedback_uses_the_api_tha: Haptic feedback uses the API that needs no VIBRATE permission. Clipboard history works because the platform delivers clipboard changes to the input method that currently has focus, which needs no permission either.
privacy_in_a_password_field_or_when: In a password field, or when an app asks for no personalised learning, there is no learning, no clipboard history and no assistant. The suggestion strip says so while it is happening.
privacy_it_would_store_a_hash_of: It would store a hash of the app's name against learned language weights. That is a behavioural profile, however small and however local, so it is opt-in and can be deleted.
privacy_no_internet_permission_and_no_ht: No INTERNET permission, and no HTTP client anywhere in the dependency graph. The build fails if either appears — including through a library that brings one in without asking.
privacy_no_telemetry_no_crash_reporting_: No telemetry, no crash reporting, no identifiers
privacy_none_of_it_exists_to_be: None of it exists to be switched off.
privacy_nothing_is_learned_in_a_password: Nothing is learned in a password field
privacy_pairs_of_words_you_write_togethe: Pairs of words you write together
privacy_per_app_language_memory_is_off: Per-app language memory is off unless you turn it on
privacy_read_from_the_installed_package_: Read from the installed package just now, not from a string in this screen. If a permission were ever added, this list would say so.
privacy_so_that_after_vreau_it_can: Learns which words you tend to write together, so the next one can be suggested sooner. Stored encrypted, never in a password field, and cleared along with the personal dictionary.
privacy_that_is_why_nothing_downloads_di: That is why nothing downloads. Dictionaries and models are either inside the app or chosen by you from a file on this device.
process_text_needs_borderkeys_as_the_key: The draft box needs BorderKeys to be the keyboard in use. Choose it below, then try again.
quick_buttons_note: Up to ten, in the order you put them. The first is the one nearest the edge the bar starts from.
quick_mode_note: Open, the bar is always there and always costs its height. As one button, it opens when tapped and closes again as soon as you choose something — which is what makes it cheap on a screen where you are only typing.
quick_placement_note: A bar down the side takes width from the keys rather than height from the screen. Worth it on a tall phone, expensive on a narrow one.
quick_show_note: A row of buttons for the things that otherwise take several gestures — copying a word, pasting, selecting everything.
resize_hint: Drag the handles to size the keyboard
setup_a_real_text_field_whatever_you: A real text field. Whatever you type here stays on this screen.
setup_android_will_warn_that_a_keyboard: Android will warn that a keyboard can read everything you type. That warning is shown for every keyboard and it is correct. What makes it a smaller risk here is that this one holds no permissions and has no way to send anything anywhere — which the Privacy screen explains and you can verify.
setup_done_borderkeys_appears_in_the_sys: Done. BorderKeys appears in the system's list of input methods.
setup_done_borderkeys_is_the_current_key: Done. BorderKeys is the current keyboard.
setup_enabled_but_not_selected_the_picke: Enabled but not selected. The picker below switches between the keyboards you have enabled.
setup_import_note: BorderKeys is installed on this device. Take them across and it will ask that application directly — it shows you what is being requested and hands it straight back, with nothing written to a file. Reading a file in is the way round when the other application is already gone.
setup_remove_note: Everything worth keeping is here now. The old application can go — the system will ask you to confirm. Its own settings and dictionary go with it, so do this after checking that what came across is what you expected.
setup_taken: Brought across. The two keep learning separately from now on.
setup_this_field_is_not_saved_anywhere: This field is not saved anywhere.
shortcuts_add: Add a shortcut to the home screen
shortcuts_enter: Hold the enter key — opens the panel inside the keyboard
shortcuts_globe: Hold the globe or the settings key, when the layout has one — opens the panel inside the keyboard
shortcuts_space: Slide along the space bar — moves the cursor
shortcuts_space_hold: Hold the space bar — switches to the next layout
shortcuts_suggestion: Hold a suggestion — offers to forget the word
shortcuts_unsupported: This launcher does not accept pinned shortcuts.
size_a_phone_number_field_gets_a: A phone number or numeric field switches to a number pad automatically.
size_an_arrow_in_the_empty_strip: An arrow in the empty strip, so the keyboard can change sides with the thumb that is already there.
size_bigger_keys_are_easier_to_hit: Bigger keys are easier to hit and leave less of the app visible. There is no right answer; there is only the one that fits your thumb.
size_blurs_the_application_behind_the_em: Blurs the application behind the empty strip. Off by default: the system composites it on every frame the keyboard is visible, and some devices refuse it outright.
size_costs_about_a_fifth_of_the: Costs about a fifth of the keyboard's height. Without it, the digits sit on the long press of the top letter row.
size_emoji_key_note: A key beside the space bar that opens the emoji grid. Off removes it and widens the space bar.
size_key_sound_note: A short click at each key press, at your phone's own touch-sound volume. Needs the system's touch sounds on too.
size_language_key_note: A key beside the space bar that cycles this keyboard's layouts. Off removes it and widens the space bar; holding the space bar does the same thing.
size_lifts_the_keyboard_off_the_bottom: Lifts the keyboard off the bottom of the screen — useful next to a gesture bar, or when the app puts something under it.
size_one_handed_mode_narrows_the_keyboar: One-handed mode narrows the keyboard and pushes it to one side, so every key is inside a thumb's arc. Left and right are separate settings rather than a handedness switch, because people change hands.
size_resize_by_hand: Or drag the keyboard itself: open the keyboard's own panel and choose “Resize by hand”.
size_space_cursor: Slide the space bar to move the cursor
size_space_cursor_note: Slide left or right on the space bar to move the cursor, without your finger covering the text.
sound_haptic_feedback_note: A light vibration each time you tap a key.
strip_private: Private field — nothing is learned or saved
swipe_a_real_field_nothing_typed_into: A real field. Nothing typed into it is saved.
swipe_all_of_it_runs_on_this: All of it runs on this device, in about a tenth of a millisecond, and the free build contains no machine-learning model of any kind.
swipe_drag_across_the_letters_instead_of: Drag across the letters instead of tapping them.
swipe_swipe_typing_is_currently_off_so: Swipe typing is currently off, so none of the above is running.
swipe_the_colour_is_on_the_theme: The colour is on the Theme screen, next to the rest of the palette.
swipe_your_gesture_is_smoothed_reduced_t: Your gesture is smoothed, reduced to sixty-four evenly spaced points, and compared against the ideal path through each candidate word's keys — once for its shape with position and size normalised away, and once for where it actually happened on the keyboard. Shape alone cannot separate two words that trace almost the same figure in different places.
theme_a_hairline_border_helps_when_the: A hairline border. Helps when the key and background colours are close.
theme_auto_follow_system_note: Switches between this theme and a separate light theme as the phone's own dark/light setting changes, instead of always showing one theme picked by hand.
theme_fill_the_correction_chip_note: Off draws a thin outline around the word a delimiter would apply -- the chip's own colour still shows through. On paints the colour below behind it instead, a filled chip rather than a traced one.
theme_follow_system_colours_note: Recolours the keyboard to match your wallpaper. Your saved colours below return the moment this is off. Needs Android 12 or newer.
theme_full_width_background_note: Keeps the surface under the keys reaching both edges of the screen, so a narrowed keyboard sits on it instead of leaving a gap.
theme_picture_dim_note: Key labels are one colour and a photograph is every colour. Without darkening, the letters vanish over whichever part of the picture is behind them.
theme_picture_note: A photograph behind the keys, kept inside this application and shrunk to what a keyboard can show. It layers with everything else: a colour underneath, the picture over it, the patterns on top.
theme_presets_note: A preset sets every colour at once. Change anything afterwards and it stays changed; the preset is a starting point, not a mode.
theme_second_colour_note: Set it to the same colour as the background for a flat surface, or to a different one for a gradient from the top of the keyboard to its bottom.
theme_values_are_clamped_when_they_are: Values are clamped when they are read, so a theme file edited by hand cannot produce a keyboard taller than the screen with the settings hidden behind it.
transfer_asking: %s is asking for what this keyboard knows, so it can carry on where this one left off.
transfer_note: It is signed with the same certificate as this build, which is why the request is being shown at all. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it, and what is sent goes straight to that application — never to a file anything else can read.
